_note: Hand-curated scheme knowledge base. Every entry carries a source_url; the scheme assistant must cite entries by id and may not add facts outside this file. Eligibility and document lists are summaries — always confirm against the source URL, since scheme rules change.

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (Jan Aushadhi)
schemes.summary: A central government programme that sells quality generic medicines at much lower prices through dedicated Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Prices are set well below the branded market rate and the medicines are tested for quality.
eligibility: Open to everyone
No card, income proof or registration needed
schemes.how_to_claim: Walk into any Jan Aushadhi Kendra and ask for the generic version of your medicine by its salt name. Use the Jan Aushadhi Sugam app or the store locator on the programme website to find your nearest Kendra.

schemes.title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
schemes.summary: Health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospital treatment at empanelled public and private hospitals. Treatment is cashless at the hospital; medicines during the hospital stay are included in the package.
eligibility: Families identified as deprived in the SECC 2011 database, and listed occupational categories
Beneficiary status can be checked on the PM-JAY portal or at a Common Service Centre
Senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered under the Vay Vandana expansion
documents: Aadhaar or another government photo ID
schemes.how_to_claim: Check eligibility on the PM-JAY website or at an empanelled hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk, get the Ayushman card made, then show it at the hospital before admission.

schemes.title: Ayushman Vay Vandana (70+ senior citizens)
schemes.summary: An expansion of PM-JAY that gives every citizen aged 70 and above cover for hospital treatment, regardless of family income.
eligibility: Age 70 years or above
Income is not a condition
schemes.how_to_claim: Register on the Ayushman app or portal, or at an empanelled hospital, to get the Vay Vandana card.

schemes.title: Free Drugs Service Initiative (National Health Mission)
schemes.summary: Under the National Health Mission, states provide essential medicines free of cost at government health facilities — from sub-centres and health and wellness centres up to district hospitals. The exact medicine list is set by each state.
eligibility: Anyone treated at a government health facility
No income test
documents: Prescription written by the government doctor
schemes.how_to_claim: Get your prescription from the government doctor and collect the medicines from the facility's drug counter or dispensary. Ask for the state Essential Drug List if a medicine is said to be unavailable.
covers: diagnostics under the free diagnostics initiative

schemes.title: Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN)
schemes.summary: Financial assistance to patients living below the poverty line who are suffering from major life-threatening diseases, for treatment at designated government super-speciality hospitals.
eligibility: Family living below the poverty line
Life-threatening illness needing super-speciality treatment
Treatment at a government hospital or institute
documents: Medical estimate and case summary from the treating government hospital
schemes.how_to_claim: The treating government hospital's medical superintendent forwards the application with a cost estimate to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare or the state's RAN fund.

schemes.title: Health Minister's Cancer Patient Fund (HMCPF)
schemes.summary: A fund within Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi dedicated to poor cancer patients, with revolving funds placed at regional cancer centres so help can be released quickly.
eligibility: Cancer diagnosis
Household income below the limit set for the fund
Treatment at a recognised regional cancer centre
schemes.how_to_claim: Apply through the regional cancer centre treating you; the centre can sanction assistance from its revolving fund.

schemes.title: Health Minister's Discretionary Grant (HMDG)
schemes.summary: A one-time grant for poor patients to help with the cost of treatment for specified serious conditions at government hospitals, where the cost is beyond the family's means.
eligibility: Annual family income below the ceiling notified for the grant
Treatment at a government hospital
documents: Medical estimate from the government hospital
schemes.how_to_claim: Submit the prescribed application through the treating government hospital to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme
schemes.summary: Free haemodialysis for patients with kidney failure at district hospitals, provided under the National Health Mission in partnership with service providers.
eligibility: Diagnosed kidney failure needing dialysis
Treatment at a participating district hospital dialysis unit
Priority for BPL families
documents: BPL or ration card where priority applies
schemes.how_to_claim: Register at the dialysis unit of your district hospital; the hospital schedules the sessions.

schemes.title: AMRIT Pharmacy (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment)
schemes.summary: Pharmacies inside major government hospitals that sell cancer and cardiovascular medicines, implants and other high-cost drugs at a steep discount to the market price.
eligibility: Open to any patient
No income test
schemes.how_to_claim: Buy directly at the AMRIT outlet in the hospital where you are being treated.

schemes.title: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD)
schemes.summary: Free screening and treatment for hypertension, diabetes and common cancers at health and wellness centres and NCD clinics, including free supply of the listed medicines.
eligibility: Anyone aged 30 and above for screening
Treatment at a government health and wellness centre or NCD clinic
schemes.how_to_claim: Visit your nearest health and wellness centre or district NCD clinic for screening, then collect the prescribed medicines from the facility.

schemes.title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (TB nutrition support)
schemes.summary: Direct benefit transfer to every notified tuberculosis patient for nutritional support, for the whole duration of treatment. TB medicines themselves are free under the National TB Elimination Programme.
eligibility: Notified TB patient under treatment
Bank account linked for the transfer
schemes.how_to_claim: Your TB treatment centre registers you on the Ni-kshay portal; the amount is credited to your bank account monthly.

schemes.title: National TB Elimination Programme — free anti-TB medicines
schemes.summary: All first-line and second-line anti-tuberculosis medicines are given free of charge at government DOTS and TB centres, including drug-resistant TB regimens.
eligibility: Diagnosed TB, treated at a government TB centre or a notified private provider under the programme
schemes.how_to_claim: Register at the nearest district TB centre or DOTS centre; medicines are dispensed free for the full course.

schemes.title: Jan Aushadhi Suvidha Sanitary Napkins
schemes.summary: Oxo-biodegradable sanitary napkins sold at ₹1 per pad at Jan Aushadhi Kendras, to make menstrual hygiene affordable.
eligibility: Open to everyone
schemes.how_to_claim: Ask for Suvidha napkins at any Jan Aushadhi Kendra.

schemes.title: Jan Aushadhi Sugam app
schemes.summary: A free government app that finds the nearest Jan Aushadhi Kendra, searches generic medicines by name and shows the price difference against the branded equivalent.
eligibility: Anyone with an Android or iOS phone
schemes.how_to_claim: Install 'Janaushadhi Sugam' from your phone's app store, allow location access and search for your medicine.

schemes.title: ESIC medical benefit
schemes.summary: Insured workers and their families get medical care, including medicines, at ESIC dispensaries and hospitals, funded by employer and employee contributions.
eligibility: Employee covered under the ESI Act through their workplace
Wages within the ESI coverage limit
documents: ESIC insurance number or Pehchan card
schemes.how_to_claim: Go to your allotted ESIC dispensary or hospital; treatment and medicines are provided against your insurance number.

schemes.title: Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan (Uttar Pradesh)
schemes.summary: A state scheme in Uttar Pradesh that extends PM-JAY-style hospital cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year to families left out of the central list.
eligibility: Resident of Uttar Pradesh
Family in the state-identified category not covered by PM-JAY
Verify your name on the state portal or at a CSC
schemes.how_to_claim: Get the Ayushman or state card made at a Common Service Centre or empanelled hospital, then use it at an empanelled hospital.

schemes.title: Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (medical assistance)
schemes.summary: Partial assistance from the PMNRF towards the cost of major medical treatment such as heart surgery, kidney transplant, cancer treatment and acid-attack care, for people who cannot afford it.
eligibility: Unable to meet the treatment cost
Treatment at a government or recognised hospital
schemes.how_to_claim: Submit the application with the hospital's cost estimate through the PMO's PMNRF portal or by post.
